proposed_from.topic:
The sharp global-treatment-effect frontier on random regular networks. For each integer n and d with nd even and 1<=d<n, G is drawn uniformly from the simple labeled d-regular graphs on [n], independently before the experiment and fully revealed. The asymptotic claim covers every admissible sequence d=d_n with d_n tending to infinity and d_n/sqrt(n) tending to zero. Constants in the risk equivalence are universal across such sequences. Probability of the asserted graph event tends to one along every such sequence. Exactly M(G,tau_GATE,2) in Kandiros-Harshaw-Savje (2026): fixed real potential-outcome schedules y_i(z) depend arbitrarily on z restricted to the closed neighborhood of i. Write y_i1=y_i(1^n) and y_i0=y_i(0^n). Require n^-1 sum_i y_ia^2<=1 for each a=0,1. No restrictions on irrelevant exposures, no bounded-degree interference order or additive response restriction. The schedule is fixed before treatment randomization; it may depend on the revealed graph. The experimenter selects any distribution D on {0,1}^n using G but no potential outcomes, then observes (Z,y(Z)). Estimators are all measurable functions of (G,Z,y(Z)); independent randomization is allowed. The minimax benchmark ranges over all such designs and estimators. tau_GATE(y)=n^-1 sum_i [y_i(1^n)-y_i(0^n)]. Risk R_2(G)=inf_(D,T) sup_(y in M(G,tau_GATE,2)) E_D[(T(G,Z,y(Z))-tau_GATE(y))^2], with any estimator randomization included. Determine an explicit evaluable deterministic scale r(n,d)>0, including every logarithmic factor, and prove universal 0<c<C<infinity such that P_G(c r(n,d)<=R_2(G)<=C r(n,d)) tends to one along every admissible d_n tending to infinity with d_n=o(sqrt(n)). The scale may not be defined as R_2 or as the original uncomputed minimax game. Whether it equals d/n, d^2/n, or an intermediate scale is answer-open. Give a total, implementable graph-dependent randomized design and estimator whose worst-case design MSE is at most C r(n,d) on the same high-probability graph event. Specify a finite sampling/evaluation algorithm and its time and memory cost; polynomial efficiency is desirable but not assumed as a second conjecture. If the computation is super-polynomial, supply an evaluable small-instance implementation and say so. Prove the lower bound against all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable estimators on the exact same published outcome class and revealed-graph experiment. A lower bound for CGD, cluster designs, linear estimators, or an assumed graph invariant does not suffice. A narrower hand-picked graph family, a risk bracket with a polynomial/log gap, an oracle estimator, or a positive result resting on an assumed lower certificate does not satisfy this kernel. Constants, designs, priors, truncation and proof mechanics are delegated. No requirement that one particular conjectured rate survive. This is an explicit same-framing retry of CausalSmith/doc/research/_bank/failed/exp_randomregular_fullgate_minimax_frontier_v1 (reraise_status: retry), not a new internal problem. The archived derivation proves a d^2/[n log(d+1)] all-procedure lower edge and d^2/n seed-design upper certificate. It does not solve the matched frontier. Three solve rounds stopped at a uniform Boolean radius-two operator/covariance bound. The new work must solve that bottleneck or derive a genuinely different attaining design or stronger all-procedure converse; reproducing the bracket is failure. External focused searches found no closure; active restricted-design topics are distinct. Consumer: Karrer et al., Network experimentation at scale (2020/2021), https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.08591, describes the deployed Facebook cluster-randomized framework for global treatment effects and two case studies. The theorem would give its global-rollout design question a sharp precision benchmark in the diffuse regular-network regime: how sample requirements grow with degree and whether an alternative design can improve over the current CGD d^2/n benchmark. Random regular graphs are a declared benchmark, not an assumption asserted about Facebook data. Eckles-Karrer-Ugander (JCI 2017), https://doi.org/10.1515/jci-2015-0021, studies the same global treatment contrast and design bias-variance tradeoff.
PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The archived attempt established only a logarithmic risk bracket. This presolve derives a new sparse-range radius-two collision tail on the uniform simple regular law and combines it with a published adjacency spectral bound. For the remaining denser range, an exact fourth-trace decomposition reduces the sufficient operator estimate to one signed four-distinct-vertex reachability moment, rather than an unbounded Boolean matrix expansion. Exhaustive enumeration of the 70 labeled cubic graphs on six vertices and 19,355 on eight vertices checks the rational probability identities and covariance algebra; these finite checks do not prove asymptotics. A separate deterministic covariance calculation supplies a weaker alternative certificate and identifies a necessary operator scale for this seed-estimator spine only.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the uniform signed four-vertex moment bound in the original dense subrange, retaining cancellations, shared witnesses and residual-degree dependence; independently audit the displayed sparse switching proof and inherited lower and seed arguments.
EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the exact eight-vertex moment identity, then bound its signed five-probability combination by a four-root switching calculation. A failed sufficient moment route must be distinguished from failure of the full answer-open minimax problem; check the weaker covariance certificate before abandoning the design.

proposed_from.novelty_justification: This is a field-tier closure of KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax Corollary 5.4, the sole theorem-level comparator, on exactly the same graph draw, estimand, endpoint \(L^2\) class, and unrestricted procedure space. The strict delta is a constant-factor characterization \(R_2(G_n)\asymp d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) with an attaining total one-shot procedure. The balanced all-procedure converse, seed and Rao--Blackwell construction, exhaustive finite compiler, and enumeration checks are inherited from \texttt{exp\_randomregular\_fullgate\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} and are not new contributions. The sparse Boolean estimate is a separately audited supporting lemma. The sole genuinely new root-level mathematical obligation is the dense signed four-root switching estimate that closes the inherited logarithmic gap. KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, UganderYin2023RGCR, CookGoldsteinJohnson2018, Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, AbbeBoixRalliSandon2020, CooperEtAl2002RandomRegular, and HarshawSavjeWang2022Riesz inform components of the argument but are not claimed to be sharpened, beaten, or extended.

seed_details.anchor: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Introduction, Proposition 2.2, Corollary 5.4, Appendix E.4, and Conclusion; failed parent proposal, logarithmic-gap review finding
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the archived unbounded Boolean inclusion--exclusion expansion by the exact fourth-trace partition and bound the combined four-root reachability cumulant by switchings before taking absolute values.
seed_details.target_method_search: Exact searches for random-regular GATE minimax risk, Boolean radius-two spectra, and signed four-root reachability found the anchor bracket, polynomial graph-matrix results, and an ongoing restricted talk, but no same-class matched theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax because its conflict graph for GATE is the two-hop graph and random regular graphs have controlled adjacency spectrum.
seed_details.rebuttal: The anchor itself obtains only \(d_n/n\) versus \(d_n^2/n\); adjacency spectral control does not control the thresholded radius-two covariance, and the signed four-root remainder is absent from its proof.

seed_details.seed: Ellipsoidal conflict-game saddle and typical evaluation
seed_details.anchor: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Proposition 2.2 and Conclusion; HarshawSavjeWang2022Riesz, estimator construction and necessity results
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the sign-schedule extreme-point reduction available for bounded outcomes by an ellipsoidal complete-class or least-favourable-prior reduction for the two empirical \(L^2\) endpoint balls.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches for an exact finite saddle for network-experiment \(L^2\) minimax risk found conflict-graph invariance and linear Riesz estimators, but no proof that linear or unbiased rules are minimax-complete.
seed_details.red_team: Finite minimax duality makes the exact risk an immediate convex program.
seed_details.rebuttal: The adversary has unbounded irrelevant exposures, the endpoint set is ellipsoidal, and estimators may be biased and nonlinear; a finite lossless reduction is precisely the missing theorem, not a routine invocation of duality.

seed_details.anchor: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4; KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Use graph-computable codegree and radius-two collision summaries to select between a low-codegree seed law and conflict resolution, then certify the selected two-arm covariance rather than analyzing one fixed design.
seed_details.target_method_search: The Li--Li public slides analyze a related low-codegree one-arm Horvitz--Thompson construction but list the full two-arm estimator as ongoing; no archival all-procedure theorem occupies the exact target.
seed_details.red_team: The January 2026 Li--Li talk already proves the pseudo-random graph frontier.
seed_details.rebuttal: Its displayed upper theorem is for one endpoint, its model bounds the full outcome vector under every assignment, and its lower comparison is restricted to Horvitz--Thompson variance rather than the present all-estimator risk.

seed_details.anchor: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, design-adaptive Le Cam construction; CooperEtAl2002RandomRegular, independence-number switching and enumeration
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Couple the two endpoint priors assignment by assignment and count balanced opposite-colour radius-two holes rather than one-colour independent sets.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches for balanced treated-control closed-neighborhood packing on random regular graphs found ordinary independence asymptotics but no two-arm information theorem.
seed_details.red_team: CooperEtAl2002RandomRegular gives the needed packing size after squaring the degree.
seed_details.rebuttal: Ordinary independence forbids all close pairs, whereas balanced exposure forbids only opposite-arm pairs and must be linked to Bayes risk for arbitrary biased estimators.
seed_details.dropped_reason: The failed parent already derived this lower edge; without a matching upper construction it reproduces the rejected logarithmic bracket.

seed_details.seed: Direct Schur-covariance certificate without a global operator bound
seed_details.anchor: KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, covariance-operator proof; failed parent proposal, exact Schur-power seed identity
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Isolate the diagonal and first Schur power in the seed covariance and control only the graph-computable off-diagonal squared-row statistic.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches for Schur-power covariance bounds for full-neighborhood exposure found fixed-design variance analyses but no random-regular certificate at the logarithmic scale.
seed_details.red_team: The Schur product theorem and a Taylor expansion immediately give the required covariance norm.
seed_details.rebuttal: They reduce the target to bounds on the maximum entry and squared-row mass, but those quantities still require uniform random-regular collision control near \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\).
seed_details.dropped_reason: It remains the fallback route inside the selected seed rather than a distinct theorem-level kernel.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Combine reachability diagrams into centered Boolean cumulants before applying block-value switchings, rather than treating each fixed polynomial shape separately.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches for thresholded graph-matrix norms on growing-degree uniform regular graphs found polynomial-shape theorems but no Boolean radius-two extension.
seed_details.red_team: Approximate the indicator by a polynomial and invoke Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices term by term.
seed_details.rebuttal: The codegree is not uniformly bounded and the required polynomial degree grows, so termwise bounds reintroduce the archived unbounded-shape summation and lose cancellation.
seed_details.dropped_reason: As a standalone graph theorem it lacks the all-procedure causal lower bound and attaining experimental design required by the topic.

seed_details.anchor: UganderYin2023RGCR, Section 3, Theorem 4.8, and Conclusion; KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Randomize the decomposition and seed count jointly so that both endpoint exposure probabilities are integrated over the clustering law before the minimax covariance bound.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches found randomized graph clustering and exact exposure integration, but no two-arm random-regular minimax guarantee under endpoint-only \(L^2\) control.
seed_details.red_team: UganderYin2023RGCR already integrates over random clusterings and yields the desired GATE variance improvement.
seed_details.rebuttal: Its theorem assumes bounded outcomes and restricted metric growth and remains an Horvitz--Thompson analysis; no matching converse over all designs and estimators is supplied.
seed_details.dropped_reason: No evidence yet shows that randomized clustering removes the simultaneous two-arm exposure obstruction rather than changing constants.

seed_details.seed: Powered-graph spectral transfer to the regular dense range
seed_details.anchor: AbbeBoixRalliSandon2020, Corollary 1, Section 2.2, and conclusion; CookGoldsteinJohnson2018, Theorem 1.1
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace sparse independent-edge tangle bounds by direct uniform-simple residual-degree switchings for Boolean radius two.
seed_details.target_method_search: The destination search found Boolean graph powering for sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'{e}nyi graphs and adjacency spectra for regular graphs, but no theorem combining both in the required dense range.
seed_details.red_team: Set the powering radius to two in AbbeBoixRalliSandon2020 and import CookGoldsteinJohnson2018 for the base spectrum.
seed_details.rebuttal: The powering theorem's displayed small-radius condition fails once \(d_n\ge n^{2/5}\), and an adjacency bound does not transfer through entrywise thresholding.
seed_details.dropped_reason: The available theorems miss exactly the degree range carrying the selected seed's open content.

proposed_from.literature_map: The selected thread starts from KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax. Its Introduction defines minimax optimality over all graph-adaptive designs and estimators, Proposition 2.2 makes risk a conflict-graph functional, Corollary 5.4 leaves the exact random-regular GATE interval \(d_n/n\) to \(d_n^2/n\), Appendix E.4 uses short-cycle counts, and the Conclusion asks for an exact characterization and improved designs. KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, Introduction, Algorithm 1, Theorem 4.1, and Conclusion, provides randomized conflict resolution, modified Horvitz--Thompson weights, and an operator-norm variance proof at \(\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\), while explicitly leaving optimality open. CookGoldsteinJohnson2018 Theorem 1.1 supplies direct uniform-simple \(O(\sqrt d)\) adjacency spectral control through \(d=O(n^{2/3})\). Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices provides the closest switching trace method for fixed polynomial shapes, but not thresholded reachability. AbbeBoixRalliSandon2020 supplies the Boolean graph-powering distinction, but its sparse small-radius theorem excludes the dense target range. UganderYin2023RGCR provides randomized decompositions and exact integration over exposure probabilities, but under bounded outcomes and a fixed estimator. CooperEtAl2002RandomRegular gives ordinary independence asymptotics, not balanced signed packing. HarshawSavjeWang2022Riesz gives unbiasedness and consistency characterizations for linear design-based estimators, not a complete class for the unrestricted game. Focused searches through September 9, 2026 found no archival paper that evaluates this exact minimax risk or proves the four-root moment. The Li--Li January 2026 public slides are the closest non-archival development; their displayed upper result is one-arm and their full two-arm construction remains ongoing.
